sections.heading: Did You Know?
paragraph: When one reused password is exposed in a breach, attackers can try it on email, banking, shopping, and other accounts.
A password manager creates and stores a different password for each account, so you do not have to remember them all.
Recovery codes and backup sign-in methods can prevent lockouts if a phone or security key is lost.

sections.heading: Who This Helps
paragraph: This service is for anyone who reuses passwords, has trouble tracking accounts, or wants stronger protection against account takeovers.
It also helps families and small businesses share access safely instead of sending passwords through text messages or unsecured notes.

sections.heading: Signs Your Password Setup Needs Work
items: You reuse the same password or a small variation across several accounts
Passwords are stored in unsecured notes, documents, or messages
You do not know which accounts use multi-factor authentication
You received a breach alert or suspicious sign-in notice and do not know what to change first
Shared accounts and recovery codes are not organized

sections.heading: What We Do
paragraph: We replace risky password habits with a practical system that works across your devices.
items: Set up a reputable password manager on supported devices
Import existing passwords and identify weak, reused, or exposed entries
Prioritize email, banking, shopping, and other important accounts
Enable multi-factor authentication and organize recovery codes
Set up secure sharing for family members or trusted helpers when needed

sections.heading: When Another Service May Be a Better Fit
paragraph: Choose Password Manager Setup and Account Security when passwords, sign-ins, account recovery, or multi-factor authentication are the main concern. For suspicious calls, messages, or fraud, choose [Scam and Fraud Protection](/services/scam-protection). If the computer may be infected, choose [Virus and Malware Removal](/services/virus-removal) first.

sections.heading: Local Availability

faq.question: Do I have to change every password at once?
faq.answer: No. Start with email, banking, shopping, and accounts that can reset other passwords. The remaining accounts can be updated in manageable groups.

faq.question: Can you help me choose and set up a password manager?
faq.answer: Yes. We can recommend an established option that supports your devices, configure it, and show you how to use sharing and recovery features.

faq.question: Will you help with multi-factor authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. We can enable it on supported accounts and organize backup methods and recovery codes to reduce the risk of a lockout.
